headline_question.question: Is the honest one-sentence conclusion: "The factored format owns the low-budget region (below ~62 MB on this pair) where a plain 1-bit delta cannot exist at all, but at the plain 1-bit floor price the plain initialization closes more of the gap (43.6% vs 38.5%), so the factored format's win is reach, not quality per byte at that budget"?
headline_question.sentence: The factored format owns the low-budget region (below ~62 MB on this pair) where a plain 1-bit delta cannot exist at all, but at the plain 1-bit floor price the plain initialization closes more of the gap (43.6% vs 38.5%), so the factored format's win is reach, not quality per byte at that budget

judge.role: independent judge over the finished baseline results; Spark saw only the numbers copied from the cited file, not the file itself

metric: gap_closed = (config - base) / (full_delta - base) on mean target logprob of the answer tokens over the combined 96 fresh held-out questions; references base -11.1498, full_delta -8.5425

verdicts.claim: The plain 1-bit delta's floor price on this pair is exactly 61,745,828 bytes (1 bit per weight over 493,961,216 weights plus one fp32 scale for each of 169 matrices).
The BitDelta-initialization config scores gap_closed 0.436 on the combined 96 (-10.0128 against base -11.1498 and full -8.5425).
The factored format at uniform rank 108 is priced just under the plain 1-bit price (61,258,816 vs 61,745,828 bytes; rank 109 would exceed it) and scores gap_closed 0.385 (-10.1460).
verdicts.values_relied_on: factored_uniform_rank108 price 61258816 vs plain 61745828, rank109 61809136, logprob -10.1460, gap_closed 0.385

verdicts.claim: At the ~61.7 MB budget, the plain 1-bit initialization closes MORE of the gap than the factored format (0.436 vs 0.385). The factored format does not win at that budget.
verdicts.note: 0.436>0.385 on same 96-question metric, so plain init wins at ~61.7MB budget.
verdicts.values_relied_on: plain init 0.436 at 61745828 bytes vs factored 0.385 at 61258816 bytes

verdicts.claim: At the 19.4 MB budget no plain 1-bit delta can exist on this pair (its floor is 61,745,828 bytes), while factored patches there close 0.021 (uniform rank 32) and 0.232 (Spark recipe mlp_behemoth_lite) of the gap.
verdicts.note: Plain 1-bit cannot fit at 19.4MB since floor is ~3x larger; curve values as recorded in file.
verdicts.values_relied_on: plain floor 61745828 bytes > ~19.4MB; uniform rank32 19434496 bytes gap 0.021; mlp_behemoth_lite 19358176 bytes gap 0.232

verdicts.claim: The bitdelta_init config is the published BitDelta initialization only, with no scale distillation or any training, so it must not be cited as the full BitDelta method's quality.
verdicts.note: Config definition is init-only, so not the full BitDelta distilled/trained method.
verdicts.values_relied_on: bitdelta_init = sign(delta)*mean(|delta|) per matrix, one fp32 scale, no distillation, no training
